verdict.rationale: The evidence only shows OpenTofu encrypting state and plan files at rest, locally and in backends, with an AES-GCM method. That keeps secrets that land in state or plan files from sitting in plaintext. It covers protection at rest, not how secrets are passed into deployments or kept out of code and logs. Missing for 10: documented sensitive or ephemeral input variables, redaction of secret values in plan/apply output and logs, integration with external secret stores, and independent hands-on corroboration that encryption keeps secrets safe.
